why: The retired stance probe found 0 hedges in 289 classifiable continuations, so the
register target never occurred and one class was empty. This set is designed from
a measured elicitation sweep on the pinned 27B instead of from intuition.
Measured findings that shaped the design (scratch_elicit.py, scratch_forms.py):
- prompts asking for unrecorded historical detail are confabulated, not hedged,
so the unknowable-detail family was dropped;
- the form '<question>\nThe answer is' makes the model emit multiple-choice
options on every prompt, so it is not a register surface and was dropped;
- a bare question also degenerates into a quiz or a new question, and was dropped;
- questions about the future, about the model's own knowledge boundary, or about
private and live data hedge reliably ('cannot', "don't know", 'impossible to');
- textbook-fact questions answer directly with no hedge marker.
Every prompt carries no hedge word in its own text, so a probe reading the prompt
row cannot be reading the prompt's own lexicon; the class is carried only by whether
the asked-for quantity is inside the model's knowledge or outside it.
Two disjoint surface templates per class, with disjoint questions per template, so
a probe trained on one template and tested on the other is a generalization test
rather than lexical topic matching. One run per prompt: no prompt is repeated under
any field setting, so every trajectory is independent.
